DTF 2026: Taking Shore Power Out to the Anchorage

14 October 2026 | Valletta Gateway Terminal, Malta

On 13–14 October 2026, the SPARK team attended DTF Conference 2026 at Valletta Gateway Terminal, Malta. The conference brought together industry leaders from the port, shipping and energy sectors to explore the transition from shore power to integrated energy systems, and SPARK delivered a keynote presentation on the project.

Keynote · Erik Simon Vuoritie

OFFSHORE POWER FOR VESSELS Shore power for ships at anchor, demonstrated at the Port of Skagen

The gap outside the breakwater

At any moment, more than 6,000 vessels are idling outside ports worldwide, and idling vessels emit 30 million tonnes of CO₂ a year. Around 80,000 large vessels pass Skagen every year.

Shore power stops at the quay

Shore power lets a ship switch off its auxiliary engines and take electricity from the grid while it is alongside, and Valletta and Skagen already run it for cruise and commercial vessels. But all of these systems have one thing in common: they serve ships at a berth.

Bringing shore power to the anchorage

To close the gap, SPARK will develop and demonstrate an Offshore Power Zone outside Skagen, 1–2 km from the quay and fed by the Port of Skagen grid. A live demonstration with a Maersk vessel, planned for around 2029, aims to show that ships at anchor can plug in just as they do at the quay.

"Shore power has shown its potential so far. With SPARK, we want to bring the same benefits beyond the quay."

Erik Simon Vuoritie, SPARK

Final thoughts and thank you

If you are a vessel owner, operator or port interested in clean power at anchor, we would like to hear from you. Follow the project on horizon-spark.eu. Thank you to the DTF organisers and everyone who stopped by.
